root_cause: R6e two-phase gather: NUM_FOLDERS=min(C,K)=7 does NOT divide C=8, so folder 0 owns 2 rows but folders 1-6 own 1. cb_gather push amount (owned*K) differs across folders, so their write pointers do NOT wrap to base uniformly. The gather-push uses get_write_ptr(cb_gather) as a remote-address proxy, which assumes uniform base across all cores (writer header lines 17-20). Divergent pointers -> NoC writes land at wrong/OOB addresses -> corruption -> nan.
fix: Fix B: make all folders reserve/push/pop cb_gather at the uniform full depth MAX_OWNED*K = ceil(C_ROWS/NUM_FOLDERS)*K (fold only actual owned rows). Restores uniform wrap-to-base. 8x8 perf target byte-identical (MAX_OWNED=1 there).

root_cause: two-phase fold: num_folders=min(C,K)=7 does not divide C=8 -> folder 0 owns 2 rows, folders 1-6 own 1 -> non-uniform cb_gather advance -> fixed-base cross-core write pointers desync after round 0 -> gather-push lands partials in stale slots -> fold sums garbage -> rsqrt(neg)=NaN

change: rms_norm_program_descriptor.py: num_folders = largest divisor of C that is <= min(C,K); two_phase engages only when >=2. Guarantees uniform ownership -> cb_gather wraps each round -> fixed-base invariant holds. Named perf targets (4x4 K=4, 8x8 K=8) unchanged (already divisors, byte-identical).
